title: Foundations: Southern Rap - The Complete Guide
summary: What Southern Rap is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Southern Rap songs: Hip-hop is rhythm and poetry: MCs rhyming over breakbeats, built from funk and soul samples. Born at Bronx block parties in the 1970s, it became the dominant global pop form.

History: DJ Kool Herc's 1973 Bronx parties invented the breakbeat; Grandmaster Flash, Run-DMC, and Public Enemy built the 1980s. The 1990s golden age (Nas, Biggie, Tupac) and 2000s–2010s (Jay-Z, Kanye, Kendrick) made it the culture.

How the songs work: Southern Rap favors the keys of Any — sample-based. Common forms include 16-bar verses, 8-bar hooks; Sampled loops with drum breaks. Players should master flow: riding the beat with internal rhymes first, then sampling: flipping old records into new beats. No guitars required.

title: Rapper's Delight - Southern Rap Song Study
summary: Harmonic blueprint and playing guide for Rapper's Delight by Sugarhill Gang (1979).
body:
Rapper's Delight — Sugarhill Gang, 1979. The first hip-hop hit; 15 minutes long.

HARMONIC BLUEPRINT (study chart, key of Any — sample-based):
Am | F | Am | G

This study chart uses the 'Minor vamp i–VI' progression, the Southern Rap workhorse, to map how songs like this move. Form: 16-bar verses, 8-bar hooks. Listen for the break: isolating the funkiest bars — it is the fingerprint of the style.
